title: Impact of Home-Based Learning and School Closures on Students Applying to Secondary Schools under Direct School Admission
what_it_is: Impact of Home-Based Learning and School Closures on Students Applying to Secondary Schools under Direct School Admission

sections.label: DSA exercise during COVID-19
sections.summary: The DSA exercise will proceed this year despite COVID-19, with applications accepted from mid-May to early June, similar to previous years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Despite the COVID-19 situation, the Direct School Admission or DSA exercise this year will proceed.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The timeline for just accepting the applications will be broadly similar to previous years, which is middle of May to early June.

sections.label: DSA placements and education shift
sections.summary: The education system is shifting away from over-emphasising examinations and grades, and about 3,500 DSA placements will be maintained this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: This is an important shift we are making to the entire education system, moving away from the over-emphasis on examinations and grades, and focusing on what matters to our children in the future, which is their curiosity, passion, ability to learn for life and mastery of their chosen crafts.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: We will therefore do our best to maintain the same number of DSA placements this year compared to last year, which is about 3,500 placements.

sections.label: E-interviews at primary schools
sections.summary: Students will go to their own primary school to participate in e-interviews, ensuring a common setting and equipment.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: To ensure an even playing field with a common setting and equipment for e-interviews, students will go to their own Primary school to participate in the e-interviews.

sections.label: DSA criteria and school judgement
sections.summary: Schools must use alternate criteria, weigh dedication and training, and exercise judgement this year in the absence of National School Games.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: This has the strongest semblance of objectivity, transparency and meritocracy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: But on the other hand, if we want to judge a child and bring the child into DSA at the age of 12 or 13, I think we may have to go beyond timings or grades, and to really also put some weight on the child's dedication, how hard he or she trains, and the schools have those records.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: So, the Member is right, that schools have to dig a bit deeper this year, given the circumstances; they have to come up with alternate criteria and explain them transparently to students and parents, so that they can apply to DSA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: At the same time, for students and parents, I also need all their understanding that this year, in the absence of National School Games, some of these qualitative attributes will come into play.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: And do accept that schools, principals and teachers do have to exercise judgement this year.
